dedupe_keys.name: prorail spoorwegen the dutch railway network dataset track axes switches crossings level crossings stations

description: Spoorwegen is ProRail's open dataset of the railway network of the Netherlands. It contains the track axis of every track (the centre line between the rails), the alignment centre line, switches, track crossings, level crossings, stations and kilometre referencing points placed about every 100 m along the track centre line; track features carry geographic codes, kilometre ranges, line sections and a life-cycle status, so planned designs can appear next to tracks in service. It is maintained by ProRail, the Dutch rail infrastructure manager, and published by PDOK. Coverage is national for the network managed by ProRail. The dataset is free to download under CC0 1.0 as a GeoPackage (about 39 MB, updated 15 July 2026) and through WMS, WFS and OGC API Features services. The metadata state that all tracks physically present are included, with positional accuracy better than 28 cm. It replaced an earlier railway dataset on PDOK in February 2021 and is refreshed as ProRail's database changes. Caveats: the dataset describes geometry and topology only, without speeds, signalling, electrification or timetables, which ProRail offers through other channels, and the life-cycle status must be filtered to keep only tracks in use. The dataset supports network flow and hazard exposure studies of Dutch rail, for example flood or heat exposure of track and level crossings, and complements the national road network (NWB) and railML-based timetable models catalogued here.
